messages:
jamie.support: Customer reporting widespread decrypt failures after they rotated the Azure Key Vault CMK in prod. They attempted to roll back to a previous key version but errors still happen and Key Vault logs don't show any rewrap operations. Need guidance on next steps.

alice.chen: Can you DM the tenant/subscription and vault name? Also whether this is managed HSM or standard KV. :thinking_face:

jamie.support: Sent details via DM — tenant 0x1234..., subscription 9876-abc, vault name 'acme-prod-kv'. They have soft-delete + purge-protection on. Rotation was by creating a new key version via portal.

maria.g: Important callout: creating a new key version does NOT automatically rewrap existing envelope keys. The data encryption keys (DEKs) remain encrypted with the old key/version. Rolling back a version in KV doesn't magically re-encrypt or rewrap stored DEKs.

sean.eng: Quick Q: what errors do they see? 'Key not found' vs 'unwrap failed' vs 403/401?

jamie.support: Error samples: unwrap failures in our logs and in their app: "UnwrapKey failed: 401 Unauthorized" for the service principal when calling UnwrapKey on the new version. SDKs sometimes bubble 403.

alice.chen: Check the Key Vault RBAC / access policy — under RBAC you need the crypto action permission (e.g., Microsoft.KeyVault/keys/unwrap/action). For managed HSM you need explicit crypto permissions. Also ensure the SPN is scoped to the correct subscription/resource.

maria.g: Also check diagnostic settings — Activity Log won't show crypto ops. You need KeyVault diagnostic logs (AuditEvent) forwarded to Log Analytics / Event Hub to see Wrap/Unwrap operations and the key-version used. Ask customer to enable if not present.

sean.eng: If they "rolled back" by creating an older version or swapping names, Azure semantics matter: versions are immutable. Rewrapping requires unwrapping with the old key/version and wrapping with the new one — a programmatic re-encrypt of DEKs. We do NOT do that automatically for BYOK in Redwood.

jamie.support: Customer asked whether Redwood should have rewrapped on rotation — quick answer: no, we don't rewrap customer-provided keys; the customer owns the DEK lifecycle unless they provide a new set of encrypted DEKs. We should document this more clearly.

security-bot: Incident response recommended steps: 1) Pause writes / put app in read-only if possible. 2) Snapshot current encrypted blobs and collect example DEKs (first 5). 3) Preserve KeyVault diagnostic logs + Activity logs. 4) Verify SPN permissions and attempt a manual unwrap/rewrap on samples. 5) Plan and run a controlled rewrap job.

alice.chen: Quick test snippet (note: may need REST/SDK rather than az CLI):
```
# example (pseudo)
POST https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/keys/<name>/<version>/unwrapkey?api-version=7.3
Body: { "alg": "RSA-OAEP", "value": "<base64-dek>" }
# then wrap with new key/version
POST https://<vault>.vault.azure.net/keys/<name>/<newVersion>/wrapkey?api-version=7.3
Body: { "alg": "RSA-OAEP", "value": "<base64-dek_plain>" }
```
If azure-cli lacks direct unwrap/wrap commands, use SDK or REST.

maria.g: Also confirm whether they used Access Policies (classic) vs RBAC for Key Vault. We see cases where an SPN has a role at subscription level but Key Vault is using resource-level RBAC and the binding isn't effective. Recommend explicitly granting crypto permissions at the vault scope and verifying 'wrapKey'/'unwrapKey' succeed from their SPN.

sean.eng: If diagnostic logs are missing for the timeframe of rotation, ask customer to reproduce in staging and capture a sample rewrap flow so we can validate our support tooling. Correlate timestamps to app errors.

jamie.support: I'll ask the customer to: 1) pause writes, 2) collect 5 failing DEKs + app error traces, 3) enable/forward KeyVault diagnostic logs and share a screenshot of the vault Access control / Access policies screen, and 4) provide SPN client-id + permissions scope so we can try in staging. They agreed to pause writes and will send samples. ETA: EOD today.

ops-bot: Automated note: created support-runbook/1923456789 for this thread and flagged as P1 for investigation.

alice.chen: I'll follow up by drafting a KB titled "Azure Key Vault BYOK rotation & rewrap responsibility" with an RBAC checklist and example unwrap/rewrap flow. We should also add a note in onboarding docs that Redwood does not auto-rewrap customer DEKs on key rotation.

maria.g: One last tip — for large datasets use a streaming rewrap job that retrieves encrypted DEKs, attempts unwrap with old key-version(s) until success, then wraps with the target CMK version. Keep audit logs of each DEK rewrap.

jamie.support: Thanks all — I'll post updates here after we have the sample DEKs and logs.
